title: Anchorization and selector precedence for model resolution (tag, semver, commit-hash semantics)
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: Customers can pin models in requests by tag names (e.g. stable, experimental), semver ranges (e.g. ^1.2.0), or exact commit hashes. Current runtime and SDK behaviors are underspecified for conflicts, fallbacks, and cache keys which leads to surprising changes during rollouts and poor telemetry aggregation. Goal: produce a clear, backwards-compatible specification and SDK surface that defines unambiguous precedence rules, deterministic resolution behavior, and a migration-friendly rollout path. The spec should cover: resolving multiple selectors in a single request, interpreting semver ranges together with tags, explicit hash overrides, client-side validation and warnings, server-side resolution determinism (including time-windowed alias stability), caching and KV-key construction (to avoid cache poisoning), telemetry fields for resolved id + selector, and an evaluable test matrix for edge cases. This ticket owns the API/SDK contract and runtime compatibility constraints for model anchoring semantics. Non-goals: design of model publishing workflows and registry UI; deep changes to model catalog storage layout (will be coordinated by infra).
acceptance_criteria: A written spec that lists selector types, exact precedence rules, and full examples for common combos (tag + semver, semver range + hash override, multiple tags)
SDK surface (JS + Python) that implements resolution validation and client warnings for deprecated selectors
Runtime resolution algorithm implemented behind a feature flag that passes the compatibility test matrix
End-to-end integration tests that assert cache keys include resolved model fingerprint and selection spec
Telemetry events that include selector, resolved_model_id, resolution_reason, and fallback_chain
Migration playbook for customers: how to move from tag-only to semver-aware pins without surprising rollouts
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Initial scoping and draft of precedence table. Identified ambiguity between 'latest-stable' tag and semver '^1.2.0' when both present.
2025-02-22: Prototype SDK validator added in internal-js-sdk branch feat/resolution-checks. Validator produces non-blocking warnings for ambiguous selectors.
2025-02-26: Discussed cache key strategy with infra; consensus to include resolved model fingerprint and canonical selector string in cache key to prevent cross-selector hits.
2025-03-04: Implementation spike in runtime behind feature-flag 'deterministic-anchor-v2' completed; initial tests passing locally. Preparing PR and integration test matrix.
2025-03-04: Noted performance microbenchmark: extra resolution step adds ~0.15ms median to cold-request path; acceptable under P1 constraints but will measure at scale.
design_notes: Precedence proposal (highest to lowest): 1) Exact commit hash, 2) Exact semver (1.2.3), 3) Semver ranges (caret/tilde/x ranges), 4) Explicit tag names (stable/experimental), 5) Implicit default assigned by project-level policy.

If multiple selectors are provided in a single request, evaluate in precedence order and short-circuit on the first successful resolution. If a higher-precedence selector resolves to an incompatible model (architecture/runtime mismatch), continue to next selector and record the incompatibility in resolution_reason.
Semver range resolution uses a deterministic tie-breaker: prefer highest available patch within range that is marked 'stable' in the catalog; if none, prefer highest semver overall.
Keep an alias stability window: tag->model mapping is considered stable for 5 minutes for in-flight requests to reduce flapping during rapid rollouts. Window length configurable per project.

Cache key format: <project-id>|<selector-canonicalized>|<resolved-model-fingerprint>|<runtime-profile-hash>. This prevents different selectors that resolve to same model from invalidating each other's caches while still enabling aggregation when identical.

SDK behavior: JS/Python expose Resolver.validate(selectors) that returns {valid: bool, warnings: [str], resolved_preview: optional str} and does not block by default. A strict mode will be offered to fail ambiguous requests.
Telemetry fields: selector_list, primary_selector_used, resolved_model_ref (immutable id), resolution_time_ms, fallback_steps (ordered list), resolution_feature_flag (v2/v1).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spec + SDK validators): write spec doc + unit tests; land SDK validator as non-blocking warning (2 sprints)
Phase 2 (runtime behind flag): implement resolution algorithm + cache key changes behind 'deterministic-anchor-v2' feature flag; add infra toggles (2 sprints)
Phase 3 (integration + telemetry): add end-to-end tests, dashboards for broken resolutions, and rollout to 10% traffic for selected projects (1 sprint)
Phase 4 (gradual rollout + strict mode): enable by default and ship strict SDK option for customers wanting deterministic failures (1 sprint)
Gate: require security_review_required and performance sign-off before enabling for enterprise projects.
decisions: Use commit-hash as absolute truth if provided — no server-side aliasing will override an exact hash.
Semver ranges resolved to highest qualified patch by default; prefer versions marked 'stable' in catalog when tie-breaking.
Include resolved model fingerprint in cache keys to avoid cross-selector cache hits.
Expose non-blocking validation in SDKs; strict mode opt-in for customers that want hard failures on ambiguous selectors.
Implement resolution behind a feature flag to enable safe dogfood and incremental rollout.
open_questions: Should we allow the registry to expose a 'deprecation window' for semver versions (eg. mark 1.2.3 deprecated but resolvable until X date)? If so, how does that affect precedence?
What level of metadata should be required on model publishes to safely apply semver logic (build artifacts with semver metadata)?
Do we need a server-enforced policy that forbids certain selector combos for enterprise customers (e.g. range + experimental tag)?
How should we present resolution previews in the Console without leaking internal commit hashes?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers see different resolved models during rollout leading to regressions. Mitigation: Tag stability window + telemetry and canary rollout steps + console preview.
Risk: Cache churn after changing cache key format. Mitigation: Backfill compatibility layer — accept both old and new cache keys for 2 weeks behind flag, monitor hit rates.
Risk: Increased latency due to extra resolution step. Mitigation: Optimize registry lookups, cache resolution results, and add async prefetch in SDKs where feasible.
Risk: Abusive selectors causing excessive RPCs to registry. Mitigation: impose rate limits and local SDK caching with TTL.
